transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... my supervisor basically said I had to come. We had this staff meeting the other day. Tuesday, I think. Yeah, Tuesday, because they always bring in those stale donuts from the bakery down the street on Tuesdays. I keep telling them Dunkin is right on the corner and it's way cheaper, but nobody listens to me. 

Anyway, I got really worked up in that meeting. I just started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was grabbing chairs and waving my arms around to show them how to do it, because, you know, Mrs. Higgins took a spill last month. Her son was so mad, he threatened to sue the whole facility, which is crazy because she's a sweet lady. She always gives me those little strawberry candies with the wrappers that look like actual strawberries. 

But yeah, I was doing the drill with the chairs and my arms going everywhere, and I just couldn't seem to stop. Even when folks told me to sit down and chill out, I just kept going. So... now I'm here.
Have you had a period of at least several days when your mood was unusually high or irritable?

Yeah, I mean, there are these stretches where I just feel... bright, you know? Like really fired up and everything is finally lining up perfectly. I get all this drive to get things done. Like the other day, I decided I was gonna reorganize the entire supply closet on the third floor. Because the third floor always gets neglected. The night shift up there, I swear, they just throw the bed pads wherever they feel like it. And the wipes! Don't even get me started on the wipes. We're supposed to use the aloe ones, but sometimes purchasing gets that cheap brand that smells like weird industrial soap, and it dries out my hands so bad. I had to buy this special lotion from CVS... the one with the green pump? It was on sale, buy one get one half off, which is a good deal because everything is so expensive right now. Gas is just ridiculous. 

But yeah, when I get like that, all fired up, if someone tries to slow me down or questions what I'm doing—like when my supervisor asked why I was pulling all the heavy boxes out into the hallway—I just snap. I snap way harder than I mean to. I ended up yelling at her about the aloe wipes until my throat hurt.
During those energized periods, do you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

Oh, for sure. When I'm in that zone, I can sleep maybe two or three hours, tops. I'll wake up way before dawn, just totally ready to go. And I don't think anything is wrong with it at all, you know? I'll just be sitting there in the living room while the house is still pitch dark, making all these big plans. 

Like the other morning, I was up at 3 AM mapping out how to fix the plumbing under my kitchen sink. Because my landlord, I swear, he hasn't sent maintenance over in six months. The pipe has this slow leak, and I had to put a plastic bucket under it. But it's one of those cheap buckets from the Dollar Tree, the orange ones? I went in there just to get some dish soap and ended up spending like twenty bucks on random stuff. They have those little bags of pretzels I like, the sourdough kind. You can't beat the price, even though they shrunk the bag size. Everything is shrinking these days. 

But yeah, the bucket was filling up, so I was awake making this whole schematic on a paper towel to fix the pipes myself. I wasn't even tired! Just completely rested and ready to get to work while everyone else was asleep.
During those high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations or delusions?

Well, yeah, actually. When I'm in one of those fired-up stretches, you know, only sleeping a couple hours and mapping out all my big plans... other things start happening, too. Like, I'll hear these voices calling out to me. Just calling my name, clear as day, but there's nobody around. And I get this absolute certainty that my supervisor is setting traps for me. 

Like, physical traps. Or trying to get me fired. She's always looking at me funny when I clock in. Our time clock is one of those old punch-card ones, which is ridiculous because it's 2023. We should have a fingerprint scanner or something. My buddy Mike, he works over at the Amazon warehouse, and they just scan their badges. He says the benefits there are crazy good, but you have to stand on your feet for ten hours straight. I don't know if my knees could take that. I played football in high school—well, until I dropped out in 10th grade—and I messed up my meniscus pretty bad. It still clicks when it rains. 

But yeah, I'd be hearing those calls and just knowing, deep down, she was plotting against me while I was trying to get all my projects done.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest or pleasure in almost everything?

I mean, depressed? No, not really. I don't get like... down in the dumps or whatever you want to call it. I always find something to keep me busy, even if it's just watching TV. Speaking of TV, have you seen how many commercials they cram into a half-hour show now? It's ridiculous. I was trying to watch this documentary on the History Channel about ancient Rome. The Romans, man, they really knew how to build stuff. Aqueducts and the Colosseum... they didn't even have power tools! Can you imagine trying to mix concrete by hand for something that big? 

My uncle used to do concrete work, actually. He poured the driveway for my mom's house back in like, '98. It still doesn't have a single crack in it. He said the secret is in how you cure it, keeping it wet for a few days. But he had to retire early because of his back. Concrete is heavy work. He gets disability now, but they make you jump through so many hoops just to get your check. It's like a full-time job just dealing with the paperwork. 

But yeah, no, I don't really get depressed or lose interest in things. I always got something going on.
Have these energized periods ever caused you to be hospitalized or require emergency psychiatric treatment?

Hospitalized? No, I haven't had to go to the hospital or do any emergency stuff like that. But, I mean, it definitely messed things up for me. Like, I was actually put on leave from my job at the senior center. Which is a shame because I really like the people there, well, most of them anyway. Mr. Henderson is a piece of work, always complaining about the thermostat. He wants it at 80 degrees in the middle of July! The HVAC system in that building is from like 1985, so if you even touch the dial, it just starts making this loud clanking noise. Sounded exactly like my old Ford Taurus before the transmission blew out on I-95. That tow truck cost me two hundred bucks, cash. They wouldn't even take a debit card, which is crazy to me. 

But yeah, they put me on leave. And at home, it's been rough too. My wife has had to remind me about, well, basically all my chores and doctor appointments because I am just not keeping up the way I used to. She bought this dry-erase board for the fridge to write everything down, but the markers she got are those cheap ones that dry out if you leave the cap off for five seconds. I told her we should just get Post-its. The guy who invented Post-its actually made the glue by accident, did you know that? He was trying to make a super strong adhesive and failed, but it turned out to be a billion-dollar mistake. 

So anyway, between the leave and just not keeping up, I've really pulled back from my church friends, too. I just don't go around them much right now. Honestly, I just worry whether I can safely return to my caregiving work at all. It's a lot of responsibility taking care of folks, you know?
Have you ever had the voices or beliefs about your supervisor when you were not feeling unusually energized or irritable?

Yeah, I did. There was this one stretch... it was actually pretty calm. I was sleeping normally again, not rushing around trying to do a million things at once. But for like, I don't know, several weeks, I was still hearing my name being called out of nowhere. And I was absolutely convinced that the people at work were keeping notes on me. 

Which, honestly, wouldn't surprise me with how corporate places are run these days. My cousin works in HR for a big tech company, and she says they track everything. Like, how long you're away from your keyboard, how many emails you send. It's like Big Brother. Have you ever read 1984? We had to read it in 9th grade English. Mr. Gable's class. He was this old guy who always wore sweater vests, even in May when it was sweltering. The school's AC was always breaking down, just like the one at the senior center. They finally replaced the chiller on the roof, but they had to bring in this massive crane to lift it. Took them all day, blocked off the whole street. Traffic was backed up all the way to Main Street. 

But yeah, even when I wasn't all fired up and energized, I was still hearing the voices and knowing they were taking notes on me. It didn't stop just because I was sleeping better.
Have there been any times when you heard voices or believed people were plotting against you for at least two weeks while you were not having any manic symptoms?

Well, yeah, like I was just saying a minute ago, right? There was that stretch where things were a lot calmer for me. I was sleeping more normally again, not rushing around with a million projects. 

Speaking of sleep, my wife and I actually went to look at a new mattress the other day, and man, have you seen the prices on those things? They want like two thousand dollars for a piece of foam! The salesman was trying to tell me it's infused with copper or something for cooling. Copper! I told him, buddy, I'm not trying to conduct electricity in my sleep, I just want my lower back to stop aching when I wake up. And he wouldn't leave us alone, just following us around the whole store. Reminds me of used car salesmen. You step one foot on the lot and they swarm you like vultures. My buddy Dave bought a truck last year and the guy kept trying to sell him this undercoating spray for an extra five hundred bucks. Total scam. 

But anyway, yeah, during that calm time... for several weeks, I was still hearing my name being called out, and I stayed completely convinced the people at work were keeping notes on me. Just like I mentioned. It didn't go away just because my energy leveled out and I was sleeping.
Have you ever had a time when the voices or beliefs kept going for at least two weeks even though your mood was back to normal?

Yeah, I mean, I feel like we're going in circles here a bit, doc. But yes, exactly what I was saying. There was that time when my mood was totally normal again. I was sleeping, I wasn't doing the million projects, things were just... calm. But for several weeks during that normal stretch, I was still hearing my name being called out of nowhere, and I was still 100% sure the people at work were keeping notes on me. 

It's like when you fix one thing on a car and another thing breaks, you know? Like my cousin's Honda Civic. He replaced the alternator, thought he was good to go, and two days later the water pump gives out. He was stranded on the side of Route 9 for three hours waiting for AAA. And you know how they tell you they'll be there in 45 minutes? It's never 45 minutes. They always contract it out to some local guy who's busy eating a meatball sub at the deli. I love a good meatball sub, actually. There's this place downtown, Luigi's, they make their own bread fresh every morning. The smell when you walk in there... it's incredible. You have to get there before noon though, or the line is out the door. 

But yeah, to answer your question, the voices and the note-taking stuff kept going for several weeks even though my mood was totally back to normal.
Have there ever been at least two weeks when you had the voices or the belief that people were plotting against you, but you were not having any manic symptoms at the same time?

Doc, are you... are you messing with me? I feel like I'm taking a test and I keep getting the answer wrong. Yes, exactly what I just said. For several weeks, I was completely calm. Sleeping normal, not doing the whole rushing around thing. But I still heard my name being called, and I stayed completely convinced the people at work were keeping notes on me. 

Speaking of notes, I have to write these daily care logs for the guys I look after. I'm an aide, right? And my one client, Mr. Henderson, he's a trip. He refuses to eat anything green. Thinks it's poison or something. I have to write down everything he eats, and the agency gets on my case if he doesn't get his vegetables. But what am I supposed to do, force-feed an 80-year-old man? He just sits there watching those old westerns all day long anyway. Gunsmoke, Bonanza. All those black and white shows. My grandma had a TV that was just this giant piece of wooden furniture. Took up half the living room. You had to turn a dial that made this loud clicking sound to change the channel, and there were only like four channels anyway. And the antenna! You had to wrap tin foil around the rabbit ears just to get the picture to stop rolling. People don't even know how good they have it now with the flat screens. 

But look, yes. To answer you again... even when the rushing around stopped and I was sleeping, the voices and the note-taking stuff stayed for a few weeks. Did you get it written down this time?
Have you ever had at least two full weeks of voices or paranoid beliefs while also feeling completely normal in your mood and energy?

Look, doc, I don't know how many different ways I can say this. Yes. Yes, I did. I feel like a broken record here, but yes. I had that calm stretch, right? Where I wasn't doing all the projects, my energy was normal, I was getting normal sleep. But for several weeks during that exact same time, I was still hearing my name, and I was still absolutely certain they were taking notes on me at work. 

It's like when my washing machine broke last month. The spin cycle just stopped working completely. I called this repair guy, and he kept asking me the same questions over the phone. "Is it plugged in? Is the lid closed?" I'm like, buddy, I'm 41 years old, I know how to close the lid on a washing machine. He finally comes out, charges me a hundred and fifty bucks just to look at it, and tells me the motor's shot. A hundred and fifty bucks! I could have bought a whole new machine on Craigslist for that. People practically give them away when they remodel their houses. They always want stainless steel everything now. My aunt remodeled her kitchen and put in all this stainless steel, and she spends half her day just wiping fingerprints off the fridge. It drives her crazy. 

But anyway, yes. Two full weeks, completely normal mood, but the voices and the paranoia about the notes... that stuff didn't stop. Are we good on that now?
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs around the times these symptoms happen?

No, no, I don't mess with any of that stuff. Never have. I mean, maybe a beer at a barbecue once in a blue moon, but nothing around the time all this was happening. I can't even drink coffee anymore, honestly. It makes my stomach do backflips. 

I used to drink like four cups a day when I worked at the warehouse. We had this old coffee pot in the breakroom that looked like it hadn't been washed since the nineties. The glass was all stained brown, and the burner was rusted out. But you drank it anyway because you were working those twelve-hour shifts, you know? Loading pallets. That job ruined my lower back. I went to a chiropractor for a while, Dr. Evans. Nice guy, had all these pictures of his golden retrievers in the waiting room. He cracked my back so loud once I thought he broke me in half. It felt great for about two hours, and then the pain came right back. He told me I needed to buy this special ergonomic pillow for eighty bucks. Everything's a racket, I swear. 

But yeah, to answer your question, no drugs, no alcohol, nothing like that when the voices or the other stuff was going on. Just me and my brain, I guess.
Have you ever had a period of at least a week where you felt so elevated or irritable that you were much more active or agitated than usual, beyond just being energized?

Yeah, definitely. There are these stretches where I just feel... I don't know, bright? Fired up. Like everything is finally lining up perfectly and I'm on top of the world. But then, if someone slows me down or questions what I'm doing, I just snap. Like, way harder than I mean to. 

It's kind of like how people drive on the interstate around here. You ever notice that? Everyone's going eighty miles an hour, thinking they're Mario Andretti, and then some guy in a minivan merges going forty-five. It's dangerous, is what it is. I saw this terrible wreck last winter on I-95. A semi-truck jackknifed across all three lanes because of black ice. We were stuck sitting there for four hours. Four hours! I had to pee in an empty Gatorade bottle. And the guy in the car next to me was blasting that terrible autotune rap music the whole time. You know, where they sound like robots? Whatever happened to real music? Like classic rock. Led Zeppelin, Pink Floyd. My uncle had this massive vinyl collection in his basement. Smelled like mildew and old paper down there, but he had original pressings of everything. He lost it all in a flood back in '08. Water came right up to the top step. 

But yeah, I get really fired up and active, and then if someone gets in my way, I just bite their head off. It's a real zero-to-sixty kind of thing.
Have there been times when your voices or paranoid beliefs were present for most of the illness, even when your mood episodes were not happening?

Well, I mean, if I'm really looking back at the whole thing... it's actually the opposite, I think. The high-energy spells, you know, when I've got all those big plans and that really short fuse we just talked about? Those have definitely taken up way more of this whole period than the calmer weeks have. 

It reminds me of this time I tried to fix up an old Camaro. I thought I had all the time in the world, and I was so pumped about it. I bought all these parts online. You wouldn't believe how expensive shipping is for car parts. Especially if they're coming from California. I ordered this carburetor, and the box got crushed in transit. FedEx wouldn't even refund me because they said the seller didn't pack it right. The seller blamed FedEx. It was a whole big mess. I spent like three weeks just arguing with customer service reps on the phone. They always put you on hold and play that awful elevator music. Like, who actually listens to that on purpose? It's like a xylophone and a pan flute just going in circles. My buddy Dave says they do it on purpose so you'll just hang up and stop bothering them. Dave works at a call center, so he'd know. He says half the time they're just playing Solitaire while you're talking anyway. 

But yeah, the mood stuff—the being super energized and irritable—that's been happening for the majority of the time, way more than just the voices or the paranoia by themselves.
Have there ever been at least two weeks when you were hearing voices or feeling paranoid, but you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

Yeah, actually, there was a time like that. I remember this one calmer stretch where I was finally sleeping normally again, and I wasn't rushing around trying to finish a million projects. Getting good sleep is tough for me anyway because my mattress is just completely shot. It's one of those memory foam ones, but it sags right in the middle like a taco. I bought it at one of those liquidation sales from a guy wearing the cheapest suit I've ever seen. He smelled like Drakkar Noir, which just instantly reminded me of my high school gym teacher, Mr. Hanes. Guy used to make us run laps if we even looked at him funny. 

But anyway, yeah, during that calmer stretch—which lasted for several weeks, actually—I was still hearing my name being called out of thin air. And I stayed completely convinced that the other people at work were keeping notes on me. I work as a personal care aide, and the other aides always carry around those little spiral-bound notebooks. You know, the ones where the wire gets bent and snags on your scrubs? I can't stand those. I always buy the black and white marbled composition books. They hold up way better. If you spill something on them, the pages don't just melt. I spilled half a diet soda on mine last month while I was trying to help this one client, Mr. Abernathy, get his shoes on. He insists on wearing these heavy leather loafers even though he never leaves the house. Says sneakers are for children. 

But yeah, for those few weeks, I wasn't fired up or agitated or anything, just sleeping and doing my normal routine, but the name-calling voices and the whole thing about my coworkers keeping tabs on me was still happening the whole time.
Have your hallucinations or paranoid beliefs ever continued for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressed symptoms?

Yeah, I think that's what I was just getting at, right? Like I was just saying, there was definitely that one calmer stretch that lasted for several weeks. I wasn't rushing around with a million projects, and I wasn't feeling down or depressed either. I was actually sleeping normally for once. But even with my mood totally level like that, I was still hearing my name being called out of thin air, and I stayed completely convinced that the people at work were keeping notes on me. 

It never really stopped. Speaking of work, the breakroom there is just a total disaster. This one aide, Brenda, she always brings in these plastic containers of leftover fish. Who microwaves fish in a tiny room with no windows? It's just disrespectful. The smell gets trapped in the vents and just hangs there all day. I tried bringing it up to the facility manager, but she's always hiding in her office playing Candy Crush on her iPad. You know they design those games specifically to addict you, right? My cousin spent like four hundred dollars on fake gold coins for some farm game on his phone. Four hundred dollars! He could have bought a real lawnmower for that, which he actually needs, because his grass is up to his knees. The city cited him for it last month and threatened to fine him. 

But anyway, yeah, for several weeks I was totally fine, sleeping good, no high or low mood stuff, but the name-calling and the paranoia about my coworkers keeping tabs on me were still happening the whole time.
Have the periods of elevated or irritable mood been present for most of the time since these problems started?

Yeah, I'm pretty sure I mentioned that earlier, right? If I really look back at the whole thing, the high-energy spells—you know, when I've got all those big plans and that really short fuse—those have definitely taken up way more of this whole period than the calmer weeks have. 

It's just been a lot of that wound-up feeling. Which is exhausting, honestly. Kind of like when I was trying to fix up that old Camaro I told you about. Man, I really wish I hadn't given up on that car. I ended up selling it to this guy off Craigslist for way less than I put into it. He rolled up in this beat-up tow truck that looked like it hadn't passed inspection since 1998. The guy was wearing a shirt that said "I'm with Stupid" but there was no arrow pointing anywhere. I kept trying to figure out if it was a misprint or if he just thought it was funny on its own. He paid me in cash, mostly twenty-dollar bills, and they all smelled like stale cigarette smoke and peppermint. I had to leave the money sitting out on my kitchen counter for two days just to air it out. My cat, Barnaby, kept trying to bat the bills onto the floor. Barnaby loves knocking things off counters. I can't even leave a glass of water out anymore without him turning it into a puddle. 

But yeah, to answer your question, those periods with the high energy and the irritability have definitely been present for the majority of the time since all this started. Way more than the calm times.
Have you ever had hallucinations or paranoid beliefs for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic symptoms at the same time?

Yeah, I... I thought I just went over this? Like I said, there was definitely that calmer stretch. I wasn't rushing around with all those projects, and my sleep was actually back to normal for a bit. But even during those several weeks, I was still hearing my name being called out of nowhere, and I was still totally convinced the people at work were keeping notes on me. 

It's just like I was saying about Brenda and the fish in the breakroom. You really can't trust people who don't have basic common courtesy, you know? It's like my neighbor, Todd. Todd bought this massive leaf blower, right? Gas powered, sounds like a jet engine taking off. And he decides the best time to use it is at 6:30 on a Sunday morning. Who does that? I went over there in my bathrobe to ask him to knock it off, and he just smiled and pointed at his noise-canceling headphones. He couldn't even hear me yelling at him! I ended up calling the non-emergency police line, but by the time they sent a cruiser out, he was already inside eating pancakes or whatever. The cop was this young kid, couldn't have been older than twenty-two, and he just gave me this look like I was the crazy one for being mad. 

But yeah, like I told you, even when I was feeling fine and sleeping normally for those few weeks, the voices and the note-taking stuff at work were still happening the whole time.
Have there been any times when you had the voices or paranoid beliefs while also having depressive symptoms?

Depressive symptoms? No, I don't think so. I haven't really felt down or depressed when the voices are happening, or really at all lately. I don't really get depressed like that. 

Now, my sister Marie, she gets depressed over every little thing. Like those sad animal rescue commercials, you know the ones? With the Sarah McLachlan song playing and the shivering dogs looking through the chain-link fences? She’ll just sit on her couch and bawl her eyes out, and then she ends up calling the 1-800 number and donating like fifty bucks she doesn't even have. I keep telling her, "Marie, you work part-time at a dollar store, you can't be funding the whole animal shelter by yourself." 

But she’s always been terrible with money. When we were teenagers, she spent her entire summer paycheck from the Dairy Queen on this huge collection of porcelain dolls. Creepiest things I've ever seen in my life. They all had these glassy eyes that just stared at you from the shelf, like they were watching you breathe. I used to have to throw a beach towel over them when I walked past her room to get to the bathroom. I swear one time I saw one of them blink, but Marie said I was just trying to ruin her collection. 

But, uh, anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, the depression thing. No, I haven't had the voices or the work stuff going on while feeling depressed. Just hasn't happened.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest or pleasure in almost everything?

Depressed? No, I really haven't. I mean, I don't get down like that for weeks at a time. I don't just lose interest in things. 

Actually, speaking of losing interest, you know what I completely lost interest in? That new reality show about the guys who flip storage units. The first season was great, really raw, you know? But then they started obviously planting stuff in the units. Like, who just happens to find a mint-condition 1960s Fender Stratocaster wrapped in a moving blanket under a pile of old tires? Come on. My buddy Dave—he's the guy who helped me move that couch last year—he actually went to one of those auctions once. He bought a unit for three hundred bucks thinking it was full of power tools because he saw a drill case near the front. Turns out, the drill case was empty, and the rest of the unit was just floor-to-ceiling boxes of expired phone books from 2004. Took him three trips to the dump to clear it out, and his truck smelled like mildew for a month. 

But yeah, no, I haven't had any two-week periods where I felt depressed or anything like that. Just not my thing.

doctor.question: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: I guess what brings me in is I got worked up in a staff meeting and started acting out a whole fall-prevention drill with chairs and my arms waving, and I couldn't seem to stop even when folks told me to sit down.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code, which is S022.

patient.answer:
Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... my supervisor basically said I had to come. We had this staff meeting the other day. Tuesday, I think. Yeah, Tuesday, because they always bring in those stale donuts from the bakery down the street on Tuesdays. I keep telling them Dunkin is right on the corner and it's way cheaper, but nobody listens to me. 

Anyway, I got really worked up in that meeting. I just started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was grabbing chairs and waving my arms around to show them how to do it, because, you know, Mrs. Higgins took a spill last month. Her son was so mad, he threatened to sue the whole facility, which is crazy because she's a sweet lady. She always gives me those little strawberry candies with the wrappers that look like actual strawberries. 

But yeah, I was doing the drill with the chairs and my arms going everywhere, and I just couldn't seem to stop. Even when folks told me to sit down and chill out, I just kept going. So... now I'm here.

I went in there just to get some dish soap and ended up spending like twenty bucks on random stuff. They have those little bags of pretzels I like, the sourdough kind. He says the benefits there are crazy good, but you have to stand on your feet for ten hours straight. I don't know if my knees could take that. So anyway, between the leave and just not keeping up, I've really pulled back from my church friends, too. I just don't go around them much right now. Honestly, I just worry whether I can safely return to my caregiving work at all. It's a lot of responsibility taking care of folks, you know?

I kept trying to figure out if it was a misprint or if he just thought it was funny on its own. He paid me in cash, mostly twenty-dollar bills, and they all smelled like stale cigarette smoke and peppermint. I had to leave the money sitting out on my kitchen counter for two days just to air it out. My cat, Barnaby, kept trying to bat the bills onto the floor. Barnaby loves knocking things off counters. I can't even leave a glass of water out anymore without him turning it into a puddle. 

But yeah, to answer your question, those periods with the high energy and the irritability have definitely been present for the majority of the time since all this started. Way more than the calm times.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms have ever occurred outside mood episodes, which is the key separator between schizoaffective disorder and bipolar disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you ever had hallucinations or paranoid beliefs for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic symptoms at the same time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a calmer stretch when I was sleeping more normally and wasn't rushing around with projects, but for several weeks I still heard my name being called and stayed convinced people at work were keeping notes on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is again asking if hallucinations or paranoid beliefs occurred for at least two weeks without manic symptoms, which directly corresponds to Additional Requirement 3.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I... I thought I just went over this? Like I said, there was definitely that calmer stretch. I wasn't rushing around with all those projects, and my sleep was actually back to normal for a bit. But even during those several weeks, I was still hearing my name being called out of nowhere, and I was still totally convinced the people at work were keeping notes on me. 

It's just like I was saying about Brenda and the fish in the breakroom. You really can't trust people who don't have basic common courtesy, you know? It's like my neighbor, Todd. Todd bought this massive leaf blower, right? Gas powered, sounds like a jet engine taking off. And he decides the best time to use it is at 6:30 on a Sunday morning. Who does that? I went over there in my bathrobe to ask him to knock it off, and he just smiled and pointed at his noise-canceling headphones. He couldn't even hear me yelling at him! I ended up calling the non-emergency police line, but by the time they sent a cruiser out, he was already inside eating pancakes or whatever. The cop was this young kid, couldn't have been older than twenty-two, and he just gave me this look like I was the crazy one for being mad. 

But yeah, like I told you, even when I was feeling fine and sleeping normally for those few weeks, the voices and the note-taking stuff at work were still happening the whole time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the psychotic symptoms occur only during manic episodes or also independently, to distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features and related diagnoses.
doctor.question: Have there been any times when you had the voices or paranoid beliefs while also having depressive symptoms?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the co-occurrence of psychotic symptoms and depressive symptoms, which is not covered in my symptom profile (my profile only mentions manic episodes).

patient.answer:
Depressive symptoms? No, I don't think so. I haven't really felt down or depressed when the voices are happening, or really at all lately. I don't really get depressed like that. 

Now, my sister Marie, she gets depressed over every little thing. Like those sad animal rescue commercials, you know the ones? With the Sarah McLachlan song playing and the shivering dogs looking through the chain-link fences? She’ll just sit on her couch and bawl her eyes out, and then she ends up calling the 1-800 number and donating like fifty bucks she doesn't even have. I keep telling her, "Marie, you work part-time at a dollar store, you can't be funding the whole animal shelter by yourself." 

But she’s always been terrible with money. When we were teenagers, she spent her entire summer paycheck from the Dairy Queen on this huge collection of porcelain dolls. Creepiest things I've ever seen in my life. They all had these glassy eyes that just stared at you from the shelf, like they were watching you breathe. I used to have to throw a beach towel over them when I walked past her room to get to the bathroom. I swear one time I saw one of them blink, but Marie said I was just trying to ruin her collection. 

But, uh, anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, the depression thing. No, I haven't had the voices or the work stuff going on while feeling depressed. Just hasn't happened.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there has ever been a major depressive episode, which would distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia-spectrum psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest or pleasure in almost everything?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a major depressive episode (feeling depressed or losing interest/pleasure for at least two weeks), which is not present in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Depressed? No, I really haven't. I mean, I don't get down like that for weeks at a time. I don't just lose interest in things. 

Actually, speaking of losing interest, you know what I completely lost interest in? That new reality show about the guys who flip storage units. The first season was great, really raw, you know? But then they started obviously planting stuff in the units. Like, who just happens to find a mint-condition 1960s Fender Stratocaster wrapped in a moving blanket under a pile of old tires? Come on. My buddy Dave—he's the guy who helped me move that couch last year—he actually went to one of those auctions once. He bought a unit for three hundred bucks thinking it was full of power tools because he saw a drill case near the front. Turns out, the drill case was empty, and the rest of the unit was just floor-to-ceiling boxes of expired phone books from 2004. Took him three trips to the dump to clear it out, and his truck smelled like mildew for a month. 

But yeah, no, I haven't had any two-week periods where I felt depressed or anything like that. Just not my thing.

Depressive episodes were denied, making bipolar-type more likely than depressive-type.
